items_missed: No agenda opener. The closest thing was 'I'll just get some, I can get some general info from you and we can kind of see what we can do' — it names the first step only, with no mention that pricing follows, no 10–15 minute timeframe, and no 'sound good?' confirmation. Agenda opener scored as not hit.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up. Went from 'How can I help you?' straight into availability, then straight into data collection.

No special-considerations probe — never asked about long walks, narrow hallways, or tight turns, on a job that is a washer, dryer, two dressers, an entertainment stand and a king mattress coming down from a second floor.

Never asked about parking or truck access at either end — an apartment complex at origin and a storage facility at destination, where loading-dock and gate access directly drive billable time. He captured the elevator situation but nothing else about access.
Never asked about additional stops.

No moving-stressor question. The customer opened with a last-minute request and later revealed he was double-covered because another mover had gone silent on him — real anxiety in the call, never named or addressed.

What's-included list never given. He asserted 'everything's included, so there's no additional fees' but never named gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, or tools — so the customer got the claim without the value behind it.
Disassembly/reassembly never mentioned, despite a washer and dryer needing disconnect and an entertainment stand in the inventory.

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. Biggest single miss on the call — the entire inventory is high-value, damage-prone items (washer, dryer, king mattress, two dressers) going down stairs and up an elevator.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — and this is a next-day move, so the pre-move email with the mover's photo is the exact reassurance a customer who has been ghosted by another mover needs.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — again, a customer who said 'I haven't received any schedule from them' was handed no guarantee at all on Einstein's arrival window.

Clock mechanics only half-explained. He stated the 2.5-hour minimum but never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, never explained 15-minute prorated increments past the minimum, and never sense-checked with 'does that make sense?'

Quoted $510 as a hard total — 'it's just $510 to get the full thing done' — with no overage language at all. On an hourly job with a second-floor walk-down and a fourth-floor elevator carry, that is a billing-dispute and estimate-accuracy risk if the crew runs past 2.5 hours.
Truck count never stated. He said 'for a two mover team' but never confirmed a truck was part of it.

Variables never explained as time drivers. He asked about the second floor, the stairs/elevator, the indoor unit and the fourth floor — then used none of it to explain why those things affect the estimate. Drive time between the two Plano addresses, walk distance at both ends, and appliance disconnect/reassembly time were all left unmentioned.

Save Your Ass speech absent entirely. No prep-equals-shorter-move-equals-lower-bill framing, no consolidation examples (loose items in the two dressers' drawers is the obvious one here), and no 'does that make sense?' close. The one bullet that genuinely didn't apply is the take-a-carload tip — the customer had already handled the small items ('I already got the other stuff taken care of').

Confirmation email described but not framed — 'I'll send you a confirmation over' with no BOLDED-details-at-the-top explanation and no 'reply with any corrections,' which is the cheapest accuracy check available on a next-day booking built from a spelled-out address over a bad line.
Hours and how to reach us never given. 'Just let us know we'll be here' is not a phone number, an email, or a set of hours.

Customer's name never used once. He gave 'Emanual Taylor' early in the call and Landon substituted 'man' for it about six times ('Alright, man', 'Awesome, man', 'Cool, awesome, man'). Zero of the required 3+ name uses.
Insurance never explained — no No Worries figure, no 60¢/lb baseline.

The competitor reveal went unworked. The customer said plainly 'I already booked with the mover but I haven't heard anything... I'm gonna keep you guys just in case, cause you guys actually give me like an actual schedule.' Landon answered 'Yeah, yeah for sure we get. Awesome man' and moved to hanging up — no attempt to convert a hedge into a commitment.
top_strength: Speed and close. This was a last-minute inbound and Landon ran it like one: he checked the calendar in real time ('We won't have any for today but we might have some for tomorrow. Just give me one second'), came back with a yes, gathered a full item-level inventory, priced it, offered specific start times, and asked for the booking — all in 5.1 minutes. The booking attempt itself is textbook: 'Would you be good to start at like, 8:30 AM or 9:00 AM' followed by 'we don't require any deposits and then we don't have any cancellation or like, rescheduling fees or anything like that. So I'll go ahead and I can get it booked for you now and then just send you a confirmation.' That is a specific time offer, the no-deposit differentiator, and an assumptive close stacked in one breath, and it worked. He was also genuinely patient on a hard line — 'Can you spell that? I'm sorry it's just, it's not super clear when you're saying the street name. Sorry about that' — and he verified the destination against the system rather than guessing ('actually I have 6720 Parkwood Boulevard in Plano, that's what popped up here'). His best rapport line came when the customer said it was a partial move: 'Gotcha, you can walk me through it. I'm ready.'
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: this customer told Landon exactly why he was shopping — another mover had taken his booking and gone silent — and Landon had all three Einstein differentiators sitting right there and used none of them. After the customer said 'I already booked with the mover but I haven't heard anything... you guys actually give me like an actual schedule,' the line he needed was: 'Emanual, that's the whole difference. You'll get a confirmation email today with the details in bold at the top — just reply if anything's wrong. A couple days out you get a Meet Your Mover email with your mover's photo and name, so you know exactly who's knocking. And we back the arrival window with our On-Time Guarantee — if we miss it, we start discounting immediately. Want me to lock 8:30 in and you can cancel the other guy?' That converts a hedge into a booking and does it with the differentiators instead of price. Second priority is estimate accuracy, which is a direct hit on the department goal: he committed to '$510 to get the full thing done' with zero overage language on a job with a second-floor stair carry of a washer and dryer and a fourth-floor elevator carry at the storage end. He should have said: 'The clock starts when we open the contract on-site, two-and-a-half-hour minimum, then 15-minute increments after that. With the stairs at your place and the elevator ride to the fourth floor, most jobs like this land right at the minimum, so $510 is what I'd plan on — does that make sense?' Same number, honest floor instead of a flat promise. Third: No Worries Damage Coverage was never said on a call that was entirely appliances, dressers and a king mattress — 'up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse accidental damage' is a ten-second add. Fourth, and the easiest to fix today: he got the customer's name in the first 60 seconds and then called him 'man' six times. Use the name. Finally, two things to verify in EMMA before the crew rolls tomorrow — the origin apartment number is inconsistent in the transcript (the customer said both '120' and '12210'/'1221' for 5720 Scruggs Way), and the origin elevator question got a garbled answer, so whether the second-floor items are a stair carry or an elevator carry is not actually confirmed on the job.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm, high-energy and easy to talk to — 'Gotcha, you can walk me through it. I'm ready,' an unprompted apology for the bad line, and a customer who closed with 'thank you so much' — held back from a 5 only by never once using the customer's name and by letting the ghosted-by-another-mover comment pass with 'Yeah, yeah for sure we get. Awesome man.'
